title: Fixed Longitudinal Groove Cup and Windowed Ball Core Display
description: One wholly newly authored complete static ball-track coupling-style dissected display on a common low base. A rear stub and full circular closure carry a thick cup whose near half is intentionally removed; its retained inner wall has genuine broad curved longitudinal grooves and full finite cut edges. Axially separated in front is one complete oblique bored star-like core with its own longitudinal grooves, a blunt through shaft, six whole rounded balls and one complete curved cage with real enclosed windows, continuous front/rear rings and separators. Two full grounded pedestals retain the separated cup and angled core shaft in this single illustrative pose. The old open ball bearing has two concentric circumferential races and a lower comb cage, not a closed-rear cup, changing longitudinal track profiles and angled core. The old rod end has one bored spherical member in a concave eye, not the intermediate windowed ball assembly. All visible geometry is new; no source meshes imported or a bearing merely rescaled and renamed. One complete connector display, zero scenes, four opaque constant untextured PBR materials, native metre-style Z up and full horizontal envelope centred on the base sole. The separated pieces deliberately do not purport to engage. Simplified artistic geometry, not technical assembly or manufacturing instructions. No track matching, bearing fit, contact trajectory, constant velocity, articulation, rolling, friction, lubrication, torque, load transfer, shaft compatibility, retention, manufacture, installation or mechanical safety is made or verified. Rigging animation and interaction not made.
